topic.title: Bayesian Nonparametrics and Structured Posterior Models
topic.overview: Bayesian nonparametric models let the complexity of clusters or latent features adapt to the data instead of fixing it in advance. This cluster studies mixture processes, hierarchical structure, scalable inference, and structured spaces such as graphs or trees. Parametric components still provide useful organization, while flexible priors allow the model to represent additional complexity when supported.
topic.whyItMatters: Unknown group counts and heterogeneous populations make rigid model sizes difficult to choose. Flexible priors are useful only when inference remains tractable and uncertainty reflects the relevant structural alternatives.
topic.evolution: The earlier representatives include Bayesian PCA, hierarchical mixtures, and infinite Gaussian mixtures. Later work accelerates variational and parallel Monte Carlo inference and extends nonparametric priors to graphs and power-law models. Recent examples address group-specific variables and differentiable distributions over phylogenetic trees, showing continued interest in flexible yet computable posterior structure.
openQuestions: How can scalable approximations preserve uncertainty over model complexity?
Which structural priors remain interpretable when data groups have genuinely different latent organizations?

papers.tldr: PCRP extends Chinese restaurant processes to matrix partitions with flexible inference that improves relational prediction in experiments.

papers.title: T-LoHo: A Bayesian Regularization Model for Structured Sparsity and Smoothness on Graphs
papers.tldr: T-LoHo models graph-connected sparsity and smoothness while providing Bayesian uncertainty about parameters and their clusters.

papers.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Learning for Point Processes with Spatial Homogeneity: A Spatial Analysis of NBA Shot Locations
papers.tldr: A Bayesian spatial model estimates basketball shot intensity by encouraging local similarity while preserving differences across the court.

papers.title: Streaming Inference for Infinite Feature Models
papers.tldr: The Recursive Indian Buffet Process enables efficient online inference in feature models whose number of latent features can grow.

papers.title: Conformal Frequency Estimation with Sketched Data
papers.tldr: A conformal method provides valid frequency-estimation intervals from data sketches under exchangeability, without knowing the distribution or sketch details.

papers.title: On Excess Mass Behavior in Gaussian Mixture Models with Orlicz-Wasserstein Distances
papers.tldr: Orlicz-Wasserstein analysis reveals almost polynomial posterior contraction in outlier regions despite slow overall parameter-convergence guarantees.

papers.title: A Unified View of FANOVA: A Comprehensive Bayesian Framework for Component Selection and Estimation
papers.tldr: A unified Bayesian FANOVA framework supports flexible component selection, uncertainty quantification, and connections among existing modeling approaches.

papers.title: Estimating Unknown Population Sizes Using the Hypergeometric Distribution
papers.tldr: A hypergeometric likelihood within a variational autoencoder estimates unknown population and category sizes from severely undersampled data.

papers.title: Global-Local Dirichlet Processes for Clustering Grouped Data in the Presence of Group-Specific Idiosyncratic Variables
papers.tldr: GLocal Dirichlet processes cluster grouped data using both shared and group-specific variables, with analyzed approximations and scalable inference.

papers.title: Variational Phylogenetic Inference with Products over Bipartitions
papers.tldr: A differentiable variational distribution enables full-space ultrametric tree inference with competitive accuracy and fewer gradient evaluations.
